dedupe_keys.name: oasis open data standards open exposure data oed and open results data ord for catastrophe modelling

description: Open Exposure Data (OED) is an open standard for describing insured exposure, meaning locations, buildings and their insurance terms, in the form catastrophe loss models consume; Open Results Data (ORD) standardises the loss outputs. Both form the Open Data Standards (ODS) maintained by Oasis Loss Modelling Framework with a steering committee of industry members and a technical working group including Verisk. OED was first developed by an industry working group with AIR Worldwide, which contributed its CEDE schema, and was ported from the Simplitium repository in 2020. Coverage: global, all classes of business. OED defines location, account, reinsurance info and reinsurance scope files with fields for geography, occupancy and construction codes, year built, number of storeys, values, deductibles and limits, and a versioning table that maps codes across versions. Format and access: CSV-based specification with an Excel specification workbook, SQL scripts, examples and documentation on GitHub, plus ODS Tools for validation and Parquet conversion; semantic versioning; free. Licence: CC0 1.0 for the standard and documentation, BSD 3-clause for code. Caveats: it is a schema, not exposure data, and models implement different OED versions and subsets of codes. Simulation uses: a common input format for hazard exposure and loss models of buildings and infrastructure, making portfolios portable between catastrophe models. Related records: the Oasis Loss Modelling Framework (platform-oasis-lmf) runs models on OED inputs, and the GEM Global Exposure Model (data-gem-global-exposure-model) is exposure data that can be mapped to it.
